MAP

notes.title: Merry Christmas! And yearly summary
notes.content:
Merry Christmas!

Christmas is just around the corner! We will soon be sitting down to Christmas dinner, opening presents, and remembering what we have experienced this year. 

We would like to take this opportunity to wish you a very merry and healthy Christmas. We also hope you find all the games you want under your Christmas tree and get some brand-new gaming equipment! 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/a25c6dd6243edc017a038e04c9276f394edf0725.jpg


As 2024 also comes to a close, we have a summary of our work on Tavern Ventures for you. 

Year in review 
Over the past year, we have made significant progress in the development of the project with numerous changes and improvements: 

Gameplay changes: 
We abandoned the marketplace in favor of dungeons, which added strategic depth to the game. We added combat, sabotage, and enemy squads to increase interaction between enemies. 
We added mini-games and mechanics for moving teams around the map. 

Development and optimization: 
We tested different versions of upgrades and introduced optimizations to the map, increasing its size. 
We added workstations to the kitchen and replaced icons for prospectors, dishes, and ingredients.

Interface and user experience: 
We built a completely new UI and added tooltips and toasts. 
We created a tutorial that, although outdated, was key at the show. 
We introduced keyboard shortcuts for player convenience. 

Animations and tools: 
We used Rive for animations and implemented them on the map. 
We created a map editor for the team and added analysis tools. 

Automation and technical support: 
We automated the process of building new game versions, including MacOS support. 

Events and extras: 
We participated in two events to showcase our progress. 
We added Easter eggs as a nod to the community. 

This year has been full of challenges, but also successes that have brought us closer to completing the project!

notes.title: Tavern Ventures: Chapter 3 - Tavern Crew
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/1d092dce3673d79d9de5e8681b7c94d49695bbf8.png
Want the usual? 
Sit down, and we'll tell you more about running a Tavern

Many customers mean success, but it's not as colorful as it seems. Picking up orders, preparing them in the kitchen, and then carrying them to the customer… A lot of work, right?
But it doesn't have to be that way! 
All it takes is a couple of employees and your life will become easier. Well-in a way. 

Employees
On the tavern menu, you can hire employees to do your tavern duties.
You can choose from the available waiters and cooks, but each has their preference for work. You need to pay attention to their statistics such as productivity, or how much they charge per hour. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/c77134f97bd5c98e3e725f102fe3d7af46593dc5.gif

Remember—the Tavern is a 24-hour, 7-day-a-week business that never closes, so there is a lot of work. Before you hire someone, you better think about whether you can afford the employee. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/4d6ecba0c465a5417cbb81402ca4da5dff5c9a14.png

Seekers
You can also hire seekers. They don't work in the Tavern, but they provide products with which you can prepare customer orders. 
So it's no different than you just thought - you have to spend to earn. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/528278d4285456744e702b50c40cff01dd8e02fd.gif

Seekers are the part of your crew that knows no fear. We send them out to check out rumors we've heard from customers, or they've searched some dungeons for us, and even conquered an area for us. 
Each of them has their own individual statistics, which affect the success of the mission given to them by you. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/b64fa1175a936ba157463c19662b4111dc6d40e1.png

Well, it's time for us to go,
The prospectors are just coming back and we have to see what they managed to get. 

Until the next meeting, future tavern keeper!

notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/1d092dce3673d79d9de5e8681b7c94d49695bbf8.png
We have a short announcement for you today about Tavern Ventures, but it's packed with news!

What have we been working on recently?
A lot of work is behind us, but there’s still much more to be done to make the game everything we’ve dreamed of! You can see the results of our recent efforts on the game’s STEAM page, where new screenshots have been uploaded. We encourage you to check them out, and later in this article, we'll explain exactly what has changed. 😉

Recent Updates:

 Designed and implemented action selection wheels.
 Redesigned many of the tavern management windows to make managing the tavern more enjoyable and user-friendly.
 Revamped the UI.
 Updated main game graphics.
 Changes to the mechanics of initiating conversations with tavern guests.
 Introduced a bargaining system for interactions with tavern guests.


What are we working on now?
We prefer not to make promises about future features too early. Plans can change, and no one likes being disappointed when something they were looking forward to doesn’t make it into the game, right? That’s why we are committed to honesty and transparency. We will only talk about what’s currently in progress and guaranteed to be in the game.

So, what’s next for Tavern Ventures?

 We are in the process of designing a few new characters.
 We are working on the mechanics and the guild system.
 We are working on renewing the map
Of course, these are not all the changes that will come to the game in the future, so if you are curious about what the future of the game will bring then we encourage you to add it to your wishlist and watch our announcements. We assure you that we will share any news of the game.

The game is constantly being developed so keep in mind that what we show may look different in the game's final version.

 And if you have any interesting ideas or comments, check out our Discord where we will be happy to talk :)

notes.title: Tavern Ventures: Chapter 2 - New Tavern
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/1d092dce3673d79d9de5e8681b7c94d49695bbf8.png

We see you've returned to hear about how the tavern works! So, sit down and listen.


Menu
A new tavern means a clean slate. The menu is also empty, so when customers come in and can't order food, they're not too happy. Their stomachs are growling, and there's no food.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/984b8bcdb9048f7fc8f553597ec22b023560304d.gif

So, let's start by setting up the tavern's menu. Each dish can be added to the menu, and its price can be increased or decreased. We'll show you how.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/a8f28300214e076a1eea92a1ace136b791579d6c.gif

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/0e4604b676f594ca07359a2a1864389c258d1cd6.gif

Changing the price also affects the tavern's reputation. A higher price means a lower reputation. People don't like to spend a lot of money, so they like the tavern more when prices are low. There's nothing you can do about it—that's just the way this damn world works. Each dish on the menu requires ingredients to prepare, and you can check what ingredients you have in the tavern's storage.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/d45b3a3881662158de728bfe2ff05747000cdf64.png

There's not much, but remember, this is a newly opened tavern. Everything needs to be earned, and if you keep coming here regularly, we've already got our first regular customer! Maybe you'll get a discount on beer?
See you around, adventurer!

notes.title: Tavern Ventures: Chapter 1 - The beginning of the story
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/1d092dce3673d79d9de5e8681b7c94d49695bbf8.png

We're taking you on a journey through Tavern Ventures today. So sit down comfortably at the bar and tell us what you're going to drink, and we'll let you know the first chapter of the story. Are you ready?
It started like this...

The Idea

Adventures and stories always have a beginning somewhere. 
In the world of fantasy and medievalism, the tavern is where the best ones begin. It's where friendships begin, it's where you can learn about the monster that spends the peasants' sleep, or unknowingly be targeted. This building is not only the beginning of the story but also often the end! It is to the tavern that heroes come after wandering and fighting, to drink, eat, and rest while recounting what they have just experienced... unless, of course, they died in the course of their adventure. 
The innkeeper in all these stories plays a minor role, but how much he has listened! After all, he is the one at all the trade talks and stories of the adventurers!

That's where the idea for the Tavern Ventures game came from!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/b2e07f61fffcdcb01c988f98e4089f37052c35c1.jpg

So work has begun on a game in which you play the role of an innkeeper running his tavern. We moved on to planning, creation, and intense thinking. The first characters were created, as well as concept drawings, which we are happy to present to you today.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/05ebb6b12ec8d27269ae3f8985553fe38cd73001.gif

How it turns out, however... Running a business in the Middle Ages is not the easiest thing to do. If you think that an innkeeper just pours beer and serves pigs to the table - we must disappoint you. However, we will tell you about it another time.

notes.title: Dev Blog : Navigating Game Development - Challenges, Decisions, and Updates
notes.content:
Hello adventurers!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/848060b1e23aba2177f6d558c4d3ba7e2bbcd846.jpg
Let me introduce myself: I'm Arkadiusz Fus (Fusu) from Cracow, Poland—nice to meet you!

After much deliberation about where and how to run a dev blog, I've decided to do it on Steam; let's see how it goes. I'm not one to talk much about what I do, rather, I do a lot and speak little :) Unfortunately, this hinders things like running a dev blog or managing social media, which I 'try' to manage. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/08f0031b8c2ebf0763e21e7f2903826df77319dd.png

Why do I make games? 
Because I've been making them since I was young, but this time I decided to finish something and do it as best I can, and if I can't, find someone who can. The tavern project started quite some time ago; 
I think there weren't games about taverns on the market back then, and the first project outline was in May 2019. 

Journey from Unity to JavaScript: Navigating Early Development Challenges
The first attempts were on the Unity engine with a college friend, but we failed, the entry threshold (learning C# + engine at once) was too high, so instead of prototyping the game, most of the effort went into learning the engine, so poor results, a lot of time spent, so motivation had to run out. Then I tried again on my own and with technology that I somewhat knew and liked, meaning JavaScript. And I started making a game without any engine, just on a framework that isn't necessarily meant for it, but the entry threshold is low because it focuses on Developer Experience and is therefore highly intuitive. So you could say I'm going uphill a bit because I'm not using a ready-made game engine, but on the other hand, I'm not writing everything from scratch, my 'engine' is the browser, but you have to write what, where, and how it should work, plus it has a lot of limitations, but most importantly I don't regret the choice :) 

Embracing Collaboration and Charting a Unique Path in Game Development
Somehow in May/June 2022 I decided that I would need help from people who will fill my gaps, especially graphic gaps, and from that moment you could say that I took the project seriously. I think choosing JavaScript closed my way to the broadly understood Gamedev, but in reality, I didn't want to be part of 'that' gamedev that is now on the market. I wanted to do a piece of 'gamedev' my way, where money is secondary, not primary. I'm also a gamer and will always be, so I see what most gamers like and what they don't. I try to ensure that player experiences in a given game are first and foremost. Although it's a very broad and difficult topic, it doesn't mean that you can't try to achieve it.

Balancing Integrity and Sustainability in Game Monetization
I won't surprise you if I say I don't like microtransactions, pay-to-win, or ads in games, so I won't use them in my own games :) DLC is cool, only if they really add some cool interesting content that is optional. But I also won't hide that I would like to earn money from the game (if it pays off it will be a success), to be able to do what I want on my own terms with great people who have a similar vibe. Passion is passion, but you have to eat and provide a roof over your head. 

Navigating Development Dilemmas: Full-Time Game Dev, Potential Projects, and Beta Decisions
I've been working full-time on the game for a while now, but unfortunately, that will end in a few days. Additionally, I'm facing a dilemma about whether to take on another project. This new project won't be easy, but it might have potential in the future, and I've already invested a lot of time and energy into it. It's also important to consider physical and mental health, personal life, and balancing what should be done with what we desire.

Therefore, I'm not sure if I'll be able to launch the open beta by the end of the year. Recently, I thought about skipping the closed alpha and going straight to the beta. However, I'm worried that there might be too many bugs initially, which could discourage players. In my opinion, there's nothing worse than game-breaking bugs, especially since it's my own engine, and I'm unsure how it will perform on different configurations and resolutions.

On the other hand, the sooner a large community forms, the better the chances of launching a Kickstarter campaign that would allow me to focus 100% on the game. So, these are the dilemmas I'm currently facing.

Shifting Gears: From Personal Insights to Tavern Updates
The most significant recent changes have been closely related to UX/UI. We've already implemented a lot of feedback from events that was quick to address, such as keyboard shortcuts for navigating the tavern or menu, adding more tooltips, and implementing a full animation for the waitress with our new solution. I've improved the map's performance, although it's still not perfect in my opinion. We've added floating texts, and most importantly, we are in the process of redesigning the majority of the menu views. This is currently taking the most time, but we already have something functional. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/1485556a4e569cef9ebb55c38873320967348811.png

Honestly, the new UI is impressive, making me excited to play. I can't wait to rework the rest and let you all try it out! Additionally, we are working on a mini-game for negotiating with customers, where you'll be able to choose the difficulty level of the negotiations. Depending on your effort, you'll earn corresponding rewards. I'll definitely show it once it's ready!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/978dc43c6a95c1cb30c1295df54fd3bbe63d0869.gif

Reflections from Pixel Heaven: Networking, Feedback, and Insights
We attended Pixel Heaven event in Warsaw, where we met many new people including other indie developers and received valuable feedback. It was quite a tiring event, especially since the organizers didn't quite manage it perfectly, but I'm feeling positive after it. Many people spoke highly about the graphics and animations, which was very gratifying. Of course, the feedback on UI/UX wasn't as good, but we were already aware of that! Some also mentioned that the game looks 'done,' which surprised me a bit. Perhaps when you work on something for so long, you see what's missing rather than what's already there? Hmm.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/472986c4eea27649749dd63c1ea84fa32bd752a7.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44974601/e909136c85ca38a2355001872351ac45cea86d14.jpg

P.S. I like memes!
